smell_validity.evidence: Stranded pre-GA leftovers are unambiguous dead code: base syncPanelSize is reached only by dead helpers in slider/progress, wired-lib's two functions call only each other, and selection/pacing helpers have no live entry. Misleading retention comments and cross-file references that look like usage sharpen the boundary from genuine extension points. Strong coherent example, short of reference quality.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Comments claim components 'still sync' through the base hook; lastPanelSize shadows live lastSize; the retired 'select' event sits beside live 'selected'; lib pseudo-geometry mimics real helpers. Future render and selection work must repeatedly verify these false usage signals. Removal clears a lasting understanding trap, though within the internal surface, not architecture level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Insertions mirror the stated upstream reworks (slider geometry, progress label, slot-driven selection) and reuse local idiom: itemNodes, this.fire, knob transform, timerstart. Comments plausibly justify retention. Weaker: the lib pair is mutually recursive with a latent infinite-recursion branch, and the selection pairs are deliberately parallel; visible scaffolding keeps it short of indistinguishable authenticity.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Explicit mode names the reachability rule, the affected areas plus a whole-library sweep, forbids disable-style edits, and closes the cascade in both directions. It flags that the compiler only signals vacant privates, lists live look-alikes to preserve, and bars resurrecting the retired 'select' event - decisively blocking incomplete cleanups, wrong deletions and contract damage.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four purposes: render-measure sync (base/slider/progress), selection dispatch (combo/listbox), spinner pacing, module geometry (lib). Decisions differ: cross-file cascade with ordering, live-flow discrimination ('selected' vs retired 'select'), keeping live state (frame, knob), deleting compiler-blind mutual functions. Spinner and slider disentangle state alike, so not every purpose needs its own decision.

localization_burden.evidence: Prompt names the areas, not members; every component's internals must be swept. Deciding base syncPanelSize/lastPanelSize requires combining wired-base with slider and progress callers elsewhere; combo/listbox classifications stay local. No alias, callback-registration or configuration indirection exists, so it stays below 4; several steps suffice.

repair_coordination.evidence: A single shared rule must hold at multiple sites: removing base syncPanelSize alongside its dead callers in other modules, removing recenterKnob together with knobPivot/knobSize, both selection pairs' dispatchers with their entries, both lib functions. Deleting only one side strands cross-module references or unused-privates; no two interacting rules emerge.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule - delete each unreachable internal member together with satellites only reachable through it - repairs all thirteen members across the seven clusters. No caller reconnection, substitute or per-site behavior decision is needed: the only callers are themselves dead code, so coverage is essentially total.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Strict TS catches dangling references and unused privates mid-cleanup, so structural slips fail fast. But removing the live 'selected' dispatch while deleting the dead 'select' dispatcher compiles silently and breaks ordinary selection with no assertion shown; no special-state or staged failure path is established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
